fund_006:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare for converting our outstanding SAFEs at our priced equity round's close. This is step one: pull every outstanding SAFE and side letter so we have accurate source data before modeling conversion math.

If you don't already have it, ask me for: (1) our {{vendor}} account/issuer identifier, and (2) confirmation that you should use my configured credentials to access {{vendor}}.

Actions to take:
1. Using my configured {{vendor}} credentials, query the convertible notes/SAFEs endpoint for our issuer to retrieve the full list of outstanding SAFEs and convertible notes, including holder name, investment amount, issue date, valuation cap, discount rate, and any MFN or pro-rata rights noted on the instrument.
2. Cross-check this list against our data room or any side letters I can point you to (ask me where these live if not obvious — e.g., a shared drive or document folder) to identify any side-letter terms (extra pro-rata rights, most-favored-nation clauses, board observer rights) that modify the standard SAFE terms but may not be captured in {{vendor}}'s structured data.
3. Flag any discrepancies: SAFEs in {{vendor}} with missing cap/discount data, side letters referencing SAFEs not found in {{vendor}}, or duplicate/conflicting terms.
4. Compile a clean summary table: holder, instrument type, amount, cap, discount, side-letter modifiers (if any), and source (platform vs. document).

Done looks like: a complete, reconciled list of every outstanding SAFE/note and associated side-letter term, with any gaps or conflicts clearly flagged for follow-up, ready to feed into the conversion-math modeling step.

Report back with the summary table, a list of flagged discrepancies or missing documents, and confirmation of how many instruments were pulled from {{vendor}} versus found only in side letters.

fund_006:n2.prompt:
You are helping me model how our outstanding SAFEs (and any convertible notes) convert into preferred stock as part of closing our priced equity round. If you don't already have them, ask me for: (1) all signed SAFE/note documents and any side letters (especially pro-rata rights), (2) the priced round terms (price per share, pre-money valuation, new money raised, option pool top-up target), and (3) access to our {{vendor}} equity-management account with our configured credentials.

Using {{vendor}}'s scenario-modeling capability, build a conversion model that: pulls in each SAFE/note's principal, valuation cap, and discount rate; calculates each holder's conversion price as the lower of the cap-based price and the discount-based price per the round terms; computes resulting share counts and resulting ownership percentage for every SAFE/note holder; incorporates any pro-rata rights from side letters into the pro-forma ownership; and models the option pool top-up alongside the new investor and founder dilution so the full pro-forma cap table is visible.

Produce a clear summary showing, per holder: instrument type, cap/discount terms, conversion price, shares issued, and resulting ownership percentage, plus the overall pro-forma cap table. Flag any SAFE or side letter terms that are ambiguous, inconsistent, or missing data needed to model conversion (e.g., unclear cap definitions, MFN clauses, conflicting pro-rata language).

Do not finalize or execute the conversion on the platform — this scenario is for review only. Package the model, the summary table, and the list of flagged ambiguities so it can be sent to counsel for confirmation of the mechanics, and stop for human sign-off before anything is executed or shared as final. Report back with the model summary, the flagged issues list, and confirmation that everything is ready for counsel review.

fund_006:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the package that outside counsel needs to confirm our SAFE conversion mechanics before the priced round closes. This is a policy-gated legal review — you must prepare all materials but stop for human sign-off before anything is sent as final or acted upon.

First, ask me for anything missing: (1) location of the signed SAFE notes and any side letters (pro-rata rights, MFN clauses, etc.), (2) the priced round term sheet or closing documents (price per share, pre-money valuation, new money raised), (3) our cap table platform/source of truth, (4) the name/email of outside counsel who will review this, and (5) any prior conversion memo or template we've used.

Then do the following: pull and organize the SAFE notes and side letters by investor, extract each note's valuation cap, discount rate, and any pro-rata or MFN terms. Build a clear conversion model spreadsheet showing, per SAFE holder: investment amount, cap, discount, calculated conversion price under each mechanism, resulting share count, and post-conversion ownership percentage. Flag any ambiguous or conflicting terms (e.g., unclear cap definitions, stacked discounts, side-letter overrides) that counsel should specifically weigh in on.

Draft a concise cover memo to counsel summarizing the round terms, listing each SAFE with its key terms and your calculated conversion outcome, and explicitly asking them to confirm or correct the mechanics before shares are issued.

Once the memo and spreadsheet are ready, stop for human sign-off — do not send the package to counsel or authorize any conversion yourself. Report back with: the draft memo, the conversion spreadsheet, a list of flagged ambiguities, and a note that counsel's written confirmation is pending and must be tracked/polled for before execution proceeds.

fund_006:n4.prompt:
You are helping me prepare for a review conversation with our lead investor about the pro-forma cap table for our priced round (all SAFEs are converting into preferred stock). Please prepare the materials I need, but do not contact the investor or negotiate on my behalf — that conversation remains a human step.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: our current cap table (from Carta, Pulley, or wherever we track it), the list of outstanding SAFEs and side letters (with caps, discounts, and any pro-rata terms), the new round's price per share and amount raised, and the lead investor's name and their intended investment amount.

Then do the following:
1. Build a clear pro-forma cap table showing: pre-round ownership, each SAFE's conversion price and resulting shares (applying cap/discount, whichever is more favorable per each SAFE's terms), the new money round's shares, and fully-diluted post-round ownership for every stakeholder including the lead investor.
2. Flag any SAFEs with pro-rata rights and show how those rights affect the lead investor's resulting percentage and any dilution they should be aware of.
3. Prepare a one-page summary in plain language: the lead investor's pre-money %, post-money %, dollars invested, and how their pro-rata rights (if any) play out.
4. List any open questions or ambiguous terms (e.g., unclear discount stacking, disputed side-letter language) that should be confirmed with counsel before the conversation.

When done, give me: the pro-forma cap table, the one-page investor summary, and the list of open questions/flags. Then stop for human sign-off — I will personally walk through and agree on the numbers with the lead investor before proceeding.

fund_006:n5.prompt:
You are helping me execute the conversion of outstanding SAFEs into preferred stock in {{vendor}}, our equity-management platform, now that our priced round has closed. If you don't already have them, ask me for: (1) the signed priced-round documents (price per share, preferred terms), (2) all outstanding SAFE notes and any side letters (caps, discounts, pro-rata rights, MFN terms), and (3) the final cap table export from {{vendor}}.

Using these inputs, do the following in {{vendor}}: model the SAFE conversion math for each note (applying cap vs. discount vs. round price, whichever yields the correct conversion price per each note's terms), and produce a pro-forma showing shares issued per SAFE holder, resulting ownership percentages, and any option pool top-up effects. Prepare draft board consents and stockholder approvals authorizing the conversions, and stage them for e-signature routing. Prepare the bulk issuance batch (all converting SAFEs as one batch upload) and draft the electronic share certificates for the new preferred stockholders, but do not submit, execute, or apply any of these — securities issuance and board consents require my explicit sign-off first.

Compile a summary package: per-holder conversion math with the source SAFE/side-letter terms cited, the draft board consent, the draft bulk issuance batch, and draft certificates, flagging any note whose terms are ambiguous or conflict with the round documents for counsel review.

When everything is prepared and internally consistent, stop for human sign-off — do not apply the conversion, issue shares, or send anything for e-signature until I explicitly approve. Report back with the pro-forma cap table, the list of prepared documents awaiting approval, and any open questions or discrepancies you found.

fund_006:n6.prompt:
You are helping me notify SAFE holders after their SAFEs converted to preferred stock in our priced round. Please draft and send individual notification emails via Gmail using my configured credentials.

Before drafting, ask me for anything missing:
1. The finalized cap table export or conversion summary (per-holder: name, email, original SAFE investment amount, conversion price, resulting share count, security type/class, and any pro-rata rights granted).
2. The company name, round name (e.g., Series Seed), closing date, and law firm/counsel name for reference.
3. Confirmation that counsel has approved the conversion mechanics and that conversions are already executed on the cap-table platform.
4. Any specific tone, disclaimers, or boilerplate legal language the company wants included (e.g., 'this is not tax advice').

Once you have this, for each SAFE holder draft a personalized email that: confirms their SAFE has converted, states the exact number and class of shares they now hold, notes the conversion price and any cap/discount applied, mentions pro-rata rights if applicable, and invites questions directed to a specified contact. Use a clear subject line like '[Company] – Your SAFE Conversion Details'.

Compile all drafts into a single document or list for my review, showing recipient, subject, and full body text. Do not send any emails yet — present the drafts and stop for human sign-off. Flag any holder records with missing or inconsistent data (e.g., no email, mismatched share counts) so I can resolve them before sending.

Report back with: the list of drafted emails ready for review, any flagged discrepancies needing my input, and a summary count of how many holders were processed successfully versus how many need follow-up.
